question: Does a 1/5/10-minute post-entry continuation check improve profit over the baseline?

universe.selection: 1h full-window coverage >= 90% AND 1m coverage >= 88% of window minutes (all qualifying symbols, no sampling)

reasons: stage-2 expansion not triggered: the user's gate requires a clear improvement on key metrics, which was not observed
no cycle passes the three gates (paired CI low > 0, FDR q < 0.10, 3/4 segments same sign)
no cycle lifts the absolute per-trade CI lower bound above zero
no cycle improves total return, expectancy and win rate together vs the same-subset baseline
10m arm sits at the 0.00 percentile of matched-rate random early exits, i.e. no selection information
stage2_decision.trigger: proceed only if a cycle passes all three gates AND absolute per-trade CI > 0

limitations: 1m coverage limits the pool to 35 symbols: of 481 symbols with full 90-day 1h bars, only 35 have >=88% 1m minutes in the window; the other 500+ have a median of 16.8 days of 1m history
the 90-day window starts 2026-08-12 and ends 2026-11-10; BTC rose over it, so short-horizon early exits carry a mechanical beta benefit
an early exit is booked at the observation bar close with the standard 0.12% round-trip cost; the baseline books barrier touches at the barrier price
the baseline uses a single full-position 3R target, whereas production supertrend_current scales out at 1R/2R/3R; absolute levels are therefore not production P&L
no funding rate, order-book depth, liquidation or partial-fill modelling; notional basis, do not subtract from margin-basis reports
observation windows of 1/5/10 minutes are far shorter than the 1.5xATR stop (mean 2.0%), so the stop is almost never touched inside the window (0.2-1.2%)
